note: Attacker-controlled Ruby String (1000 digit '9's created by ("9"*1000).to_f) enters the vulnerable function together with its full length; this is the source of the overflowing data.
Fixed 70-byte stack buffer (DBL_DIG=15 so 15*4+10=70) that receives a sanitized copy of the digits; every input digit is copied here with no capacity check.
n points at the start of buf; subsequent writes advance n past the buffer because the copy loop is bounded by the input length (pend = s + len), not by sizeof(buf).

Each of the 1000 input characters is stored through n with no check that n stays inside buf; for len=1000 the stores run ~930 bytes past the 70-byte stack buffer, which is the root cause of the stack-buffer-overflow.
NUL terminator is written at buf+1000, far beyond the 70-byte buffer, completing the out-of-bounds sequence that the sanitizer reports as a stack-buffer-overflow in mrb_str_len_to_dbl.
